application_questions.question: A hairdresser in Geelong charges $\$50$ before GST. Add $10\%$ GST ($\$5$) to find the total bill including GST.
A pair of football boots is $\$80$, and a sports store takes $25\%$ off. Calculate $25\%$ of $\$80$ ($80 \div 4$), then subtract it from $\$80$ to find the sale price.
The price of a cinema ticket rose from $\$20$ to $\$22$ (an increase of $\$2$). Calculate $\dfrac{2}{20} \times 100\%$ to find the percentage increase.
A cafe receipt in Sydney shows a GST-inclusive total of $\$33$. Divide $\$33$ by $11$ to find the GST amount included in the bill.

reasoning_questions.question: Explain how you can use $10\%$ of $\$60$ ($= \$6$) to quickly work out $5\%$ of $\$60$ and $15\%$ of $\$60$ in your head.
A shirt costs $\$100$. Its price increases by $10\%$ to $\$110$, and then $10\%$ is taken off $\$110$. Calculate $10\%$ of $\$110$ to show the final price is $\$99$, not $\$100$.
reasoning_questions.answer: $10\%$ of $\$110$ is $\$11$, so $\$110 - \$11 = \$99$ (the $10\%$ discount is taken from the larger $\$110$ amount).

application_questions.question: A bakery in Hobart makes a birthday cake for $\$20$ and sells it for $\$35$. Find (a) the dollar profit ($35 - 20$) and (b) the percentage profit $\dfrac{15}{20} \times 100\%$.
A skateboard priced at $\$60$ has a $20\%$ discount. Calculate $20\%$ of $\$60$ ($\$12$) and subtract it from $\$60$ to find the sale price.
Jack deposits $P = \$1000$ into a savings account at $r = 3\%\text{ p.a.}$ ($0.03$) for $t = 5\text{ years}$. Multiply $1000 \times 0.03 \times 5$ to find the simple interest earned.
Using Jack's investment from Question 7 ($P = \$1000, I = \$150$), calculate $A = P + I$ to find his total account balance after $5$ years.

reasoning_questions.question: To use $I = Prt$ when the interest rate is $r = 6\%\text{ p.a.}$, a student substitutes $r = 6$ instead of $r = 0.06$. Explain why this makes their answer $100$ times too large.
reasoning_questions.answer: $6\%$ means $\dfrac{6}{100} = 0.06$; using $6$ instead of $0.06$ multiplies the principal by $6$ ($600\%$) instead of $6\%$.

reasoning_questions.question: If you invest $\$500$ at $10\%\text{ p.a.}$ simple interest, you earn $\$50$ interest each year. How many years will it take to earn $\$200$ in interest?
